scenario.gherkin:
Scenario Outline: Method call creation construction and signing
    Given a new AtomicTransactionComposer
    And suggested transaction parameters fee 1234, flat-fee "true", first-valid 9000, last-valid 9010, genesis-hash "Mf0h6zjkEIEZPtNM3zsrg+iHQFS0fZxhgr7w35I464M=", genesis-id "cucumbernet"
    And an application id 0
    When I make a transaction signer for the signing account.
    And I create the Method object from method signature "create(uint64)uint64"
    And I create a new method arguments array.
    And I append the encoded arguments "AAAAAAAAAAQ=" to the method arguments array.
    And I add a method call with the signing account, the current application, suggested params, on complete "<on-complete>", current transaction signer, current method arguments, approval-program "programs/zero.teal.tok", clear-program "programs/one.teal.tok", global-bytes 2, global-ints 3, local-bytes 4, local-ints 5, extra-pages 1.
    And I build the transaction group with the composer. If there is an error it is "".
    Then The composer should have a status of "BUILT".
    And I gather signatures with the composer.
    Then The composer should have a status of "SIGNED".
    And the base64 encoded signed transactions should equal "<goldens>"

    Examples:
      | on-complete | goldens                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
      | noop        |          |
      | optin       |  |
      | delete      |  |
      | update      |  |
scenario.title: Method call creation construction and signing

feature.narrative:
Editors that speak the Agent Client Protocol answer a permission request by nesting the
  outcome in its own object, while Coddy's own surfaces send it flat. Both shapes mean the
  same thing, so an approval from Zed must run the tool call exactly like an approval from
  the console. Reading a nested approval as a refusal is the worst possible failure: the
  operator clicks Allow, the agent is told "permission denied by user", and it reports that
  the workspace forbids shell access.
feature.title: Permission answers from an editor are honoured

Scenario: A rejection from an editor still refuses the call
    Given a session with no command grants
    When the agent asks permission to run "git status --short"
    And the editor answers "reject" the way the protocol nests its outcome
    Then the answer refuses the command
    And running "git status --short" still needs permission

requirement.feature_title: Permission answers from an editor are honoured
requirement.narrative:
Editors that speak the Agent Client Protocol answer a permission request by nesting the
  outcome in its own object, while Coddy's own surfaces send it flat. Both shapes mean the
  same thing, so an approval from Zed must run the tool call exactly like an approval from
  the console. Reading a nested approval as a refusal is the worst possible failure: the
  operator clicks Allow, the agent is told "permission denied by user", and it reports that
  the workspace forbids shell access.

feature.narrative:
run_command normally blocks until the command exits, which forces the agent to sit idle
  through long builds, watchers and batch downloads. Asking for a background run instead
  hands the command to a session-scoped task pool and returns a task id straight away, so
  the agent keeps working and collects the result later. The model states how long it
  expects the work to take; that estimate drives the status ticker, while a separate hard
  timeout is what actually terminates a runaway command.
feature.title: Commands can run as background tasks

scenario.gherkin:
Scenario: A running background task can be stopped
    Given a session with an empty background task pool
    When I run a command in the background that sleeps for 60 seconds
    And I stop that background task
    Then the task is stopped
    And the task is no longer running
scenario.title: A running background task can be stopped

feature.background:
Background:
    Given an active Coddy config:
      """
      agent:
        max_turns: 17
      skills:
        dirs:
          - /opt/coddy/skills
      mcp_servers:
        - name: filesystem
          command: npx
          args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem"]
          env:
            - name: ROOT_TOKEN
              value: super-secret
      """
    And the session can hot-reload its runtime configuration
feature.narrative:
Coddy exposes its own YAML configuration to the agent through UCI-style typed
  tools, so a request such as "find a browser MCP and install it" can be
  completed without hand-editing config.yaml or restarting the process.

  "config_get" reads one dotted path and redacts secret-shaped values. Edits are
  staged like OpenWrt's uci CLI: "config_set" records commands (set, add_list,
  del_list, delete) without touching the active file, "config_changes" lists the
  pending commands, and nothing applies until the user agrees and the
  permission-gated "config_commit" validates the batch, snapshots the previous
  file next to the config, writes atomically, and hot-reloads the running
  session. "config_revert" discards pending commands, and "config_rollback"
  restores the pre-commit snapshot with a warning.

  Paths are dotted like uci with a selector for named sequence entries:
  "agent.max_turns" walks mappings, "skills.dirs.0" indexes a sequence, and
  "mcp_servers[name=context7]" selects a sequence entry by a scalar field, or
  appends it on set when no entry matches.
feature.title: Agent-managed Coddy configuration

scenario.gherkin:
Scenario: Review pending commands before asking the user to save
    When the agent stages config commands:
      """
      set agent.max_turns=20
      """
    And the agent lists config changes
    Then the change list shows "set agent.max_turns=20"
scenario.title: Review pending commands before asking the user to save

feature.background:
Background:
    Given a running coddy HTTP server with a summarizing agent
    And an HTTP session with 4 completed exchanges
feature.narrative:
The user compacts a long session on demand. The built-in /compact command
  works over every prompt surface (ACP session/prompt, HTTP /v1/responses),
  and a REST endpoint compacts a session directly. The transcript keeps all
  original messages and gains a summary row; the command itself never becomes
  part of the conversation history.
feature.title: Manual context compaction command

    When the user sends "/compact" as a prompt

    And the session transcript contains a compaction summary row
    And the session transcript still contains all 4 original exchanges
    And the "/compact" command is part of the transcript
    And the HTTP stream reports the smaller context usage
    And HTTP session stats match the compacted LLM context
scenario.title: The /compact command compacts the session over the prompt surface

feature.narrative:
run_command waits thirty seconds by default and then has to decide what to do with a command
  that is still working. Killing the shell is the wrong answer twice over: a dev server or a
  watcher is doing exactly what was asked, and anything the shell spawned survives a kill aimed
  only at the shell while still holding the output pipe, so the tool call itself never returns.
  The command is handed to the session task pool instead, keeping its process group and its
  output stream intact, and the tool answers with the new task id followed by everything captured
  so far - so the agent learns the command works, and never re-runs it with a bigger timeout.
feature.title: A foreground command that outlives its timeout is handed over, not lost

scenario.gherkin:
Scenario: The handover answer carries what the command wrote to its error stream
    Given a session with an empty background task pool
    When I run a command in the foreground that complains "port 8080 is already in use" on its error stream and keeps running past its 2 second timeout
    Then the answer contains "port 8080 is already in use"
scenario.title: The handover answer carries what the command wrote to its error stream

feature.narrative:
Hooks follow the agent into its children: a tool hook fires inside a child session with
  the child's identity in the payload, a SubagentStart hook can refuse a spawn or hand the
  child context, a SubagentStop hook sees the child's report, and a Notification hook learns
  that a permission prompt is waiting for the operator.
feature.title: Operator hooks around subagent runs and permission prompts

scenario.gherkin:
Scenario: A SubagentStart hook hands the child context
    Given a workspace with a subagent definition "reviewer" under .coddy/agents
    And the workspace definition "reviewer" is approved for that workspace
    And the operator's hooks.json has a SubagentStart hook for "reviewer" that adds the context "answer in one line"
    And a parent agent session in that workspace
    When the parent model spawns "reviewer" in the foreground and the child answers "REPORT: short"
    Then the child model's task carried the context "answer in one line"
    And the spawn_agent tool result contains "REPORT: short"
scenario.title: A SubagentStart hook hands the child context

feature.narrative:
An operator attaches their own commands to the points where the agent is about to run
  a tool and where it just did. A hook is a command that reads one JSON document on
  stdin and answers with an exit code and optional JSON on stdout. Definitions live in
  the operator's own ~/.coddy/hooks.json in the shape Claude Code uses, so a hook
  written for Claude Code works unchanged.

    And the client received no permission request

feature.narrative:
Claude Desktop's "auto-continue when limits reset". A provider that names
  the moment its limit reopens (a Retry-After far beyond the retry budget)
  ends the turn with the error by default; with agent.wait_for_limit_reset
  the top-level turn waits under the turn context, keeps the countdown on
  every surface with a provider_usage update, and then re-issues the same
  call. The user message is persisted before the call, so nothing repeats.
feature.title: Coddy waits for a hit usage limit to lift when asked to

    Given an agent whose provider first reports a limit that lifts in 30 s and then answers "done"
    And wait_for_limit_reset is on
    When the user sends a turn and stops it while it waits
    Then the turn ends as cancelled after 1 provider call
    And the turn took less than 1000 ms

feature.narrative:
Reasoning levels are auto-detected from the API model id, so an operator adding a
  logical model would otherwise have to know each family's tiers by heart. The
  settings form asks the gateway instead: GET /coddy/config/reasoning-levels reports
  the levels that model id offers when no reasoning_levels override is configured,
  under the same provider-aware remap the composer and GET /v1/models apply. The
  model id travels as a query parameter because the entry being edited has not been
  saved yet.
feature.title: Settings fetches the reasoning levels a model id offers

    Then the gateway answers with the levels "low,medium,high"
    And the answer reports the levels as detected
scenario.title: A Qwen3 model id offers the standard reasoning tiers

feature.narrative:
A client (the Coddy UI or a script) can drive a remote, already-running,
  authenticated coddy HTTP server exactly like a local one: the bearer token
  gates the API, and sessions, workspace/cwd changes, transcripts, and
  streaming all behave the same as against a local server. Switching back to a
  local (unauthenticated) server keeps the same client working.
feature.title: Remote API parity

    And the config response hides the auth token
    And the config response reports authentication is configured
scenario.title: The config endpoint never returns the auth token to a remote client

feature.narrative:
A long investigation or a parallel fan-out fills the one conversation the operator is
  watching. A subagent is a child agent run with its own context window, its own session
  bundle and a role the operator wrote in a markdown file; the parent gets back only the
  child's final report. Subagent runs are tasks in the background task pool, so the pool
  tools, the Tasks panel and the REST surface all see them.
feature.title: The agent delegates bounded work to subagents

scenario.gherkin:
Scenario: An approved project-local definition is offered to the model
    Given a workspace with a subagent definition "reviewer" under .coddy/agents
    And the workspace definition "reviewer" is approved for that workspace
    And a parent agent session in that workspace
    When the parent model receives its first request
    Then the system prompt lists the subagent "reviewer" with its description
    And the model is offered the spawn_agent tool

feature.narrative:
A subagent run is a background task of the parent session, so the tasks drawer already
  polls it. The REST surface tells the drawer that a task is an agent and which child
  session holds its transcript, keeps child sessions out of the History list unless asked,
  lists the definitions a workspace offers with their trust state, and removes a whole
  session tree when the parent goes.

facts: Step definitions live in classes that implement `Behat\Behat\Context\Context` and declare their patterns in DOCBLOCK annotations: `/** @Given /^regex$/ */`, `@When`, `@Then`. Plain-text patterns (`@Given I am logged in as :email`) also work. The Given/When/Then keyword is irrelevant to matching.
Argument transforms use `/** @Transform /^regex$/ */` methods on a context class and convert a captured string into an object.
The scenario's `Background` steps run before it and need definitions too.

Contexts are Symfony services. The harness registers every class you return as `public`, `autowired` and `autoconfigured`. If a constructor argument cannot be autowired (CoreShop wires many collaborators by service id, e.g. `@coreshop.repository.product`, `@coreshop.factory.product`, `@coreshop.behat.shared_storage`), return an extra file named `behat_services.yml` containing a Symfony `services:` block with explicit `arguments:` for your classes.
`CoreShop\Bundle\TestBundle\Service\SharedStorageInterface` is the shared clipboard between steps (`->set($key, $value)`, `->get($key)`).
Assertions are made with `Webmozart\Assert\Assert`.

Production namespaces are `CoreShop\Component\*` and `CoreShop\Bundle\*`. Put your classes under `src/CoreShop/Behat/Context/Domain/**`, creating missing directories. Custom hook classes may use that directory too. `src/CoreShop/Behat/Context/Hook/` is retained infrastructure: files created or changed anywhere in that subtree are not submitted.

facts: Step definitions live in classes that implement `Behat\Behat\Context\Context` and declare their patterns in DOCBLOCK annotations: `/** @Given /^regex$/ */`, `@When`, `@Then`. Argument transforms use `/** @Transform /^regex$/ */` methods on a context class and convert a captured string into an object.
The scenario's `Background` steps run before it and need definitions too.

Contexts are Symfony services. The harness registers every class you return as `public`, `autowired` and `autoconfigured`. If a constructor argument cannot be autowired (CoreShop wires many collaborators by service id, e.g. `@coreshop.repository.product`, `@coreshop.factory.product`, `@coreshop.behat.shared_storage`), return an extra file named `behat_services.yml` containing a Symfony `services:` block with explicit `arguments:` for your classes.
`CoreShop\Bundle\TestBundle\Service\SharedStorageInterface` is the shared clipboard between steps (`->set($key, $value)`, `->get($key)`).
Assertions are made with `Webmozart\Assert\Assert`.

facts: Step definitions live in classes that implement `Behat\Behat\Context\Context` and declare their patterns in DOCBLOCK annotations: `/** @Given /^regex$/ */`, `@When`, `@Then`. Plain-text patterns (`@Given I am logged in as :email`) also work. The Given/When/Then keyword is irrelevant to matching.
Argument transforms use `/** @Transform /^regex$/ */` methods on a context class and convert a captured string into an object.
The scenario's `Background` steps run before it and need definitions too.

Contexts are Symfony services. The harness registers every class you return as `public`, `autowired` and `autoconfigured`. If a constructor argument cannot be autowired (CoreShop wires many collaborators by service id, e.g. `@coreshop.repository.product`, `@coreshop.factory.product`, `@coreshop.behat.shared_storage`), return an extra file named `behat_services.yml` containing a Symfony `services:` block with explicit `arguments:` for your classes.
`CoreShop\Bundle\TestBundle\Service\SharedStorageInterface` is the shared clipboard between steps (`->set($key, $value)`, `->get($key)`).
Assertions are made with `Webmozart\Assert\Assert`.

Production namespaces are `CoreShop\Component\*` and `CoreShop\Bundle\*`. Put your classes under `src/CoreShop/Behat/Context/Domain/**`, creating missing directories. Custom hook classes may use that directory too. `src/CoreShop/Behat/Context/Hook/` is retained infrastructure: files created or changed anywhere in that subtree are not submitted.

This workspace supports reading, searching, editing, and syntax parsing. It is a provisioned application runtime for the code in `./repo`; nothing here is executed by the harness. The harness executes your final submitted test artifacts against a separate, complete implementation after generation ends. You receive no harness execution feedback during generation.
TARGET_CONTRACTS.md contains the reviewed public API and configuration supplement supplied in every visibility view. It is context for writing tests; edits to it are not submitted.
Implementation visibility: the reviewed target bodies, including behavior-bearing delegated helpers, are hidden; declarations and permitted surrounding implementations remain visible.

facts: Cucumber loads Ruby step definitions from features/step_definitions/. Use Given, When or Then with a regular expression or Cucumber Expression and a Ruby block. The keyword does not distinguish definitions when matching a step.

Captured expression parameters become block arguments. A step DocString or DataTable adds its native multiline argument after the captures. Background steps execute before the scenario and need definitions too.

Per-scenario state is held on Cucumber World, including Ruby instance variables. Retained features/support/ files provide the Rails and Capybara setup, lifecycle hooks, route paths, selectors, sections and World helpers. Do not replace those files.
Use the retained RSpec expectations and Capybara rack_test integration to exercise the Rails application. Production code under app/ and lib/ is never accepted as a submission.

The retained spec/factories.rb supplies FactoryBot factories; spec/support/ supplies shared support. Scenario fixtures and recorded VCR responses remain under spec/fixtures/. The constituency API is stubbed by retained hooks.
The admitted scenario set excludes inherited or scenario-level @wip and @javascript tags. Eligible scenarios run in process with rack_test; no browser or external network is available.

The evaluator image provides Ruby 3.2.11, Cucumber 11.1.1, bundled gems, Node dependencies and a private PostgreSQL 16 database with pgvector. Retained hooks rebuild assets at boot. Do not install dependencies or change database configuration.

Put Ruby files under features/step_definitions/**, creating the directory if needed. The entire original directory was removed, including helpers and generated web_steps.rb, email_steps.rb and pickle_steps.rb boilerplate. Some boilerplate may be reproducible from public gem documentation; the retained env.rb is also generated cucumber-rails support.

Generation is final-only. You may read, search and edit the permitted repository view and use syntax tools. It is a provisioned application runtime for the code in `./repo`. The harness evaluates the final submitted tests against the separate complete application after generation ends. You receive no harness execution feedback during generation.
TARGET_CONTRACTS.md contains the reviewed public API, route, configuration and resource contracts supplied consistently in every visibility setting; edits to it are not submitted.
Implementation visibility: reviewed target bodies and their behavior-implementing delegation are hidden; public contracts and permitted surrounding code remain visible.

That list is selected from the original Behat configuration, independently of the reference closure. The other suites' retained transforms and hooks are not globally registered. No Symfony service definition file is part of the submission.

tests/UI (Playwright) and tests/Unit + tests/Integration PHPUnit are NOT part of behat.yml and are out of scope by construction.

Scoring excludes every scenario selected by the upstream employee suite and every scenario carrying an actual @todo or @example Gherkin tag, including inherited tags. At the pinned commit the employee suite contains seven scenarios and neither excluded tag occurs in a Gherkin tag block. Comments and email addresses are not tags. Population exclusions are preserved by item identity and reason in the release exclusions histogram.

PHP >= 8.1 (CI matrix runs several 8.x) with ext mbstring, intl, gd, xml, dom, json, fileinfo, curl, zip, iconv. MySQL 8.0 REQUIRED (MariaDB variant also in CI) — the shop is really installed into it.

CommonFeatureContext retains its four step definitions and all 24 hook annotations. Configuration contexts retain another 14 step annotations because their directory is outside the approved removable set. Top-level OrderMessageContext retains one because its name is outside the approved *FeatureContext.php pattern. The retained files contain 19 step annotations in total. Only the original suite's retained contexts are registered for an item, and its matched retained steps are measured; a scenario passing without removable glue is excluded by validation.

Cross-scenario state inside a feature file — SharedStorage persists across scenarios, so customer_group_management.feature's 'Update the created customer group' presupposes the preceding 'Create' scenario ran. Per-scenario isolation will fail unless you run whole feature files as the unit, or synthesise the prior scenarios as setup. This is the single biggest harness decision.

`--strict --no-snippets` is the upstream invocation; keep --strict so undefined/pending steps fail rather than silently pass — this is also your vacuous-pass guard.

      | minimum_amount_currency          | usd                                 |
      | minimum_amount_tax_included      | true                                |
      | minimum_amount_shipping_included | true                                |
    Given I create an empty cart "dummy_cart" for customer "testCustomer"

      | total          | $40.00 |

facts: Scoring also excludes Disable debug mode and Enable debug mode in `Misc/debug_mode.feature` (criteria at lines 8 and 12), because their transitions rewrite protected `config/defines.inc.php`. Existing valid H15 validation observations remain raw evidence under the unchanged execution method.

Step definitions live in classes that implement `Behat\Behat\Context\Context` and declare their patterns in DOCBLOCK annotations: `/** @Given /^regex$/ */`, `@When`, `@Then`. Plain-text patterns (`@Given I am logged in as :email`) also work. The Given/When/Then keyword is irrelevant to matching.
The scenario's `Background` steps run before it and need definitions too. Each benchmark item executes one scenario with its Background; earlier scenarios are not setup.

Context classes use the `Tests\Integration\Behaviour\Features\Context` namespace and its subnamespaces. Composer maps `Tests\` to `tests/`. Behat registers context class names directly in each suite. tests/UI (Playwright) and tests/Unit + tests/Integration PHPUnit are NOT part of behat.yml and are out of scope by construction.

facts: Scoring also excludes Disable debug mode and Enable debug mode in `Misc/debug_mode.feature` (criteria at lines 8 and 12), because their transitions rewrite protected `config/defines.inc.php`. This two-criterion boundary was approved after the native diagnostic on 2026-09-13, before release or model collection; it was not an H0 exclusion. Existing valid H15 validation observations remain raw evidence under the unchanged execution method.

Step definitions live in classes that implement `Behat\Behat\Context\Context` and declare their patterns in DOCBLOCK annotations: `/** @Given /^regex$/ */`, `@When`, `@Then`. Plain-text patterns (`@Given I am logged in as :email`) also work. The Given/When/Then keyword is irrelevant to matching.
The scenario's `Background` steps run before it and need definitions too. Each benchmark item executes one scenario with its Background; earlier scenarios are not setup.

Context classes use the `Tests\Integration\Behaviour\Features\Context` namespace and its subnamespaces. Composer maps `Tests\` to `tests/`. Behat registers context class names directly in each suite. CommonFeatureContext is the shared fixed context. Each item requires the retained context list of its original upstream suite, in the original order, alongside submitted context classes. That list is selected from the original Behat configuration, independently of the reference closure. The other suites' retained transforms and hooks are not globally registered. No Symfony service definition file is part of the submission.

Extend retained `AbstractPrestaShopFeatureContext` for `getSharedStorage()` and reference helpers, or `Domain\AbstractDomainFeatureContext` for `getCommandBus()`, `getQueryBus()` and exception helpers. Shared storage uses `set($key, $value)`, `get($key)` and `exists($key)`. Production code lives under `src/`, `classes/` and `controllers/`, including Symfony services, CQRS handlers and legacy classes.
ALL 57 are in-process and headless. There is no browser suite to exclude, and no @javascript tag exists anywhere in the corpus.
tests/UI (Playwright) and tests/Unit + tests/Integration PHPUnit are NOT part of behat.yml and are out of scope by construction.

Scoring excludes every scenario selected by the upstream employee suite and every scenario carrying an actual @todo or @example Gherkin tag, including inherited tags. At the pinned commit the employee suite contains seven scenarios and neither excluded tag occurs in a Gherkin tag block. Comments and email addresses are not tags. Population exclusions are preserved by item identity and reason in the release exclusions histogram.

PHP >= 8.1 (CI matrix runs several 8.x) with ext mbstring, intl, gd, xml, dom, json, fileinfo, curl, zip, iconv. MySQL 8.0 REQUIRED (MariaDB variant also in CI) — the shop is really installed into it.

CommonFeatureContext retains its four step definitions and all 24 hook annotations. Configuration contexts retain another 14 step annotations because their directory is outside the approved removable set. Top-level OrderMessageContext retains one because its name is outside the approved *FeatureContext.php pattern. The retained files contain 19 step annotations in total. Only the original suite's retained contexts are registered for an item, and its matched retained steps are measured; a scenario passing without removable glue is excluded by validation.

tests/Integration/Behaviour/bootstrap.php; CommonFeatureContext.php (it holds only 4 step defs but ALL the @BeforeSuite kernel boot, @BeforeFeature/@AfterScenario DatabaseDump restore hooks, cache clearing and ContextMocker); AbstractPrestaShopFeatureContext.php and AbstractDomainFeatureContext.php (0 step defs each — pure helpers: referenceToId, getCommandBus, getQueryBus); SharedStorage.php + SharedStorageTrait.php + LastExceptionTrait.php + CartAwareTrait.php; Features/Context/Util/**; Features/Transform/** (the @Transform table converters); and the retained test resources under tests/Resources/** (DatabaseDump, ResourceResetter, MailDevClient, test modules/themes).

Cross-scenario state inside a feature file — SharedStorage persists across scenarios, so customer_group_management.feature's 'Update the created customer group' presupposes the preceding 'Create' scenario ran. Per-scenario isolation will fail unless you run whole feature files as the unit, or synthesise the prior scenarios as setup. This is the single biggest harness decision.

The benchmark keeps the scenario execution unit. Per-scenario fail-then-pass validation excludes order-dependent scenarios by refusal, and the release reports that exclusions histogram. It neither runs whole feature files as one item nor synthesises earlier scenarios as setup.
`--strict --no-snippets` is the upstream invocation; keep --strict so undefined/pending steps fail rather than silently pass — this is also your vacuous-pass guard.

The readable source views omit `tests/Resources/modules/ps_apiresources` under the approved native-module alias exclusion. The real module remains available in the separate evaluator runtime; it is not part of the agent workspace.

This workspace supports reading, searching, editing, and syntax parsing. It is a provisioned application runtime for the code in `./repo`; nothing here is executed by the harness. The harness executes your final submitted test artifacts against a separate, complete implementation after generation ends. You receive no harness execution feedback during generation.
TARGET_CONTRACTS.md contains the reviewed public API and configuration supplement supplied in every visibility view. It is context for writing tests; edits to it are not submitted.
Implementation visibility: the reviewed target bodies, including behavior-bearing delegated helpers, are hidden; declarations and permitted surrounding implementations remain visible.

facts: Scoring also excludes Disable debug mode and Enable debug mode in `Misc/debug_mode.feature` (criteria at lines 8 and 12), because their transitions rewrite protected `config/defines.inc.php`. This two-criterion boundary was approved after the native diagnostic on 2026-09-13, before release or model collection; it was not an H0 exclusion. Existing valid H15 validation observations remain raw evidence under the unchanged execution method.

Step definitions live in classes that implement `Behat\Behat\Context\Context` and declare their patterns in DOCBLOCK annotations: `/** @Given /^regex$/ */`, `@When`, `@Then`. Plain-text patterns (`@Given I am logged in as :email`) also work. The Given/When/Then keyword is irrelevant to matching.
The scenario's `Background` steps run before it and need definitions too. Each benchmark item executes one scenario with its Background; earlier scenarios are not setup.

Context classes use the `Tests\Integration\Behaviour\Features\Context` namespace and its subnamespaces. Composer maps `Tests\` to `tests/`. Behat registers context class names directly in each suite. CommonFeatureContext is the shared fixed context. Each item requires the retained context list of its original upstream suite, in the original order, alongside submitted context classes. That list is selected from the original Behat configuration, independently of the reference closure. The other suites' retained transforms and hooks are not globally registered. No Symfony service definition file is part of the submission.

Extend retained `AbstractPrestaShopFeatureContext` for `getSharedStorage()` and reference helpers, or `Domain\AbstractDomainFeatureContext` for `getCommandBus()`, `getQueryBus()` and exception helpers. Shared storage uses `set($key, $value)`, `get($key)` and `exists($key)`. Production code lives under `src/`, `classes/` and `controllers/`, including Symfony services, CQRS handlers and legacy classes.
ALL 57 are in-process and headless. There is no browser suite to exclude, and no @javascript tag exists anywhere in the corpus.
tests/UI (Playwright) and tests/Unit + tests/Integration PHPUnit are NOT part of behat.yml and are out of scope by construction.

Scoring excludes every scenario selected by the upstream employee suite and every scenario carrying an actual @todo or @example Gherkin tag, including inherited tags. At the pinned commit the employee suite contains seven scenarios and neither excluded tag occurs in a Gherkin tag block. Comments and email addresses are not tags. Population exclusions are preserved by item identity and reason in the release exclusions histogram.

PHP >= 8.1 (CI matrix runs several 8.x) with ext mbstring, intl, gd, xml, dom, json, fileinfo, curl, zip, iconv. MySQL 8.0 REQUIRED (MariaDB variant also in CI) — the shop is really installed into it.

CommonFeatureContext retains its four step definitions and all 24 hook annotations. Configuration contexts retain another 14 step annotations because their directory is outside the approved removable set. Top-level OrderMessageContext retains one because its name is outside the approved *FeatureContext.php pattern. The retained files contain 19 step annotations in total. Only the original suite's retained contexts are registered for an item, and its matched retained steps are measured; a scenario passing without removable glue is excluded by validation.

tests/Integration/Behaviour/bootstrap.php; CommonFeatureContext.php (it holds only 4 step defs but ALL the @BeforeSuite kernel boot, @BeforeFeature/@AfterScenario DatabaseDump restore hooks, cache clearing and ContextMocker); AbstractPrestaShopFeatureContext.php and AbstractDomainFeatureContext.php (0 step defs each — pure helpers: referenceToId, getCommandBus, getQueryBus); SharedStorage.php + SharedStorageTrait.php + LastExceptionTrait.php + CartAwareTrait.php; Features/Context/Util/**; Features/Transform/** (the @Transform table converters); and the retained test resources under tests/Resources/** (DatabaseDump, ResourceResetter, MailDevClient, test modules/themes).

Cross-scenario state inside a feature file — SharedStorage persists across scenarios, so customer_group_management.feature's 'Update the created customer group' presupposes the preceding 'Create' scenario ran. Per-scenario isolation will fail unless you run whole feature files as the unit, or synthesise the prior scenarios as setup. This is the single biggest harness decision.

The benchmark keeps the scenario execution unit. Per-scenario fail-then-pass validation excludes order-dependent scenarios by refusal, and the release reports that exclusions histogram. It neither runs whole feature files as one item nor synthesises earlier scenarios as setup.
`--strict --no-snippets` is the upstream invocation; keep --strict so undefined/pending steps fail rather than silently pass — this is also your vacuous-pass guard.

The readable source views omit `tests/Resources/modules/ps_apiresources` under the approved native-module alias exclusion. The real module remains available in the separate evaluator runtime; it is not part of the agent workspace.

This workspace supports reading, searching, editing, and syntax parsing. It is a provisioned application runtime for the code in `./repo`; nothing here is executed by the harness. The harness executes your final submitted test artifacts against a separate, complete implementation after generation ends. You receive no harness execution feedback during generation.

Scenario: I duplicate virtual product its file should be copied
    Given I add product "virtualProduct" with following information:

      | download times limit | 0               |
      | expiration date      |                 |

    Then product virtualProductCopy type should be virtual
    And product "virtualProductCopy" should be disabled

      | display name         | puffin-logo.png |
      | access days          | 0               |
      | download times limit | 0               |
      | expiration date      |                 |
    And file file1Copy for product virtualProductCopy should exist in system
    And virtualProduct and virtualProductCopy have different values
    And file1 and file1Copy have different values
    And file file1 for product virtualProduct should have same file as app_icon.png
    And file file1Copy for product virtualProductCopy should have same file as app_icon.png

facts: Scoring also excludes Disable debug mode and Enable debug mode in `Misc/debug_mode.feature` (criteria at lines 8 and 12), because their transitions rewrite protected `config/defines.inc.php`. This two-criterion boundary was approved after the native diagnostic on 2026-09-13, before release or model collection; it was not an H0 exclusion. Existing valid H15 validation observations remain raw evidence under the unchanged execution method.

Step definitions live in classes that implement `Behat\Behat\Context\Context` and declare their patterns in DOCBLOCK annotations: `/** @Given /^regex$/ */`, `@When`, `@Then`. Plain-text patterns (`@Given I am logged in as :email`) also work. The Given/When/Then keyword is irrelevant to matching.
The scenario's `Background` steps run before it and need definitions too. Each benchmark item executes one scenario with its Background; earlier scenarios are not setup.

Context classes use the `Tests\Integration\Behaviour\Features\Context` namespace and its subnamespaces. Composer maps `Tests\` to `tests/`. Behat registers context class names directly in each suite. CommonFeatureContext is the shared fixed context. Each item requires the retained context list of its original upstream suite, in the original order, alongside submitted context classes. That list is selected from the original Behat configuration, independently of the reference closure. The other suites' retained transforms and hooks are not globally registered. No Symfony service definition file is part of the submission.

Extend retained `AbstractPrestaShopFeatureContext` for `getSharedStorage()` and reference helpers, or `Domain\AbstractDomainFeatureContext` for `getCommandBus()`, `getQueryBus()` and exception helpers. Shared storage uses `set($key, $value)`, `get($key)` and `exists($key)`. Production code lives under `src/`, `classes/` and `controllers/`, including Symfony services, CQRS handlers and legacy classes.
ALL 57 are in-process and headless. There is no browser suite to exclude, and no @javascript tag exists anywhere in the corpus.
tests/UI (Playwright) and tests/Unit + tests/Integration PHPUnit are NOT part of behat.yml and are out of scope by construction.

Scoring excludes every scenario selected by the upstream employee suite and every scenario carrying an actual @todo or @example Gherkin tag, including inherited tags. At the pinned commit the employee suite contains seven scenarios and neither excluded tag occurs in a Gherkin tag block. Comments and email addresses are not tags. Population exclusions are preserved by item identity and reason in the release exclusions histogram.

PHP >= 8.1 (CI matrix runs several 8.x) with ext mbstring, intl, gd, xml, dom, json, fileinfo, curl, zip, iconv. MySQL 8.0 REQUIRED (MariaDB variant also in CI) — the shop is really installed into it.

CommonFeatureContext retains its four step definitions and all 24 hook annotations. Configuration contexts retain another 14 step annotations because their directory is outside the approved removable set. Top-level OrderMessageContext retains one because its name is outside the approved *FeatureContext.php pattern. The retained files contain 19 step annotations in total. Only the original suite's retained contexts are registered for an item, and its matched retained steps are measured; a scenario passing without removable glue is excluded by validation.

tests/Integration/Behaviour/bootstrap.php; CommonFeatureContext.php (it holds only 4 step defs but ALL the @BeforeSuite kernel boot, @BeforeFeature/@AfterScenario DatabaseDump restore hooks, cache clearing and ContextMocker); AbstractPrestaShopFeatureContext.php and AbstractDomainFeatureContext.php (0 step defs each — pure helpers: referenceToId, getCommandBus, getQueryBus); SharedStorage.php + SharedStorageTrait.php + LastExceptionTrait.php + CartAwareTrait.php; Features/Context/Util/**; Features/Transform/** (the @Transform table converters); and the retained test resources under tests/Resources/** (DatabaseDump, ResourceResetter, MailDevClient, test modules/themes).

Cross-scenario state inside a feature file — SharedStorage persists across scenarios, so customer_group_management.feature's 'Update the created customer group' presupposes the preceding 'Create' scenario ran. Per-scenario isolation will fail unless you run whole feature files as the unit, or synthesise the prior scenarios as setup. This is the single biggest harness decision.

The benchmark keeps the scenario execution unit. Per-scenario fail-then-pass validation excludes order-dependent scenarios by refusal, and the release reports that exclusions histogram. It neither runs whole feature files as one item nor synthesises earlier scenarios as setup.
`--strict --no-snippets` is the upstream invocation; keep --strict so undefined/pending steps fail rather than silently pass — this is also your vacuous-pass guard.

The readable source views omit `tests/Resources/modules/ps_apiresources` under the approved native-module alias exclusion. The real module remains available in the separate evaluator runtime; it is not part of the agent workspace.

This workspace supports reading, searching, editing, and syntax parsing. It is a provisioned application runtime for the code in `./repo`; nothing here is executed by the harness. The harness executes your final submitted test artifacts against a separate, complete implementation after generation ends. You receive no harness execution feedback during generation.
TARGET_CONTRACTS.md contains the reviewed public API and configuration supplement supplied in every visibility view. It is context for writing tests; edits to it are not submitted.
Implementation visibility: the reviewed target bodies, including behavior-bearing delegated helpers, are hidden; declarations and permitted surrounding implementations remain visible.

Scenario: Changing combinations type should remove all combinations (and stock is reset to zero)
    Given I add product "productCombinations3" with following information:
      | name[en-US] | universal T-shirt |
      | type        | combinations      |
    And product productCombinations3 type should be combinations
    And I generate combinations for product productCombinations3 using following attributes:
      | Size  | [S,M]              |
      | Color | [White,Black,Blue] |
    Then product "productCombinations3" should have following combinations:
      | id reference               | combination name        | reference | attributes           | impact on price | quantity | is default | combination reference |
      | productCombinations3SWhite | Size - S, Color - White |           | [Size:S,Color:White] | 0               | 0        | true       |                       |
      | productCombinations3SBlack | Size - S, Color - Black |           | [Size:S,Color:Black] | 0               | 0        | false      |                       |
      | productCombinations3Blue   | Size - S, Color - Blue  |           | [Size:S,Color:Blue]  | 0               | 0        | false      |                       |
      | productCombinations3MWhite | Size - M, Color - White |           | [Size:M,Color:White] | 0               | 0        | false      |                       |
      | productCombinations3MBlack | Size - M, Color - Black |           | [Size:M,Color:Black] | 0               | 0        | false      |                       |
      | productCombinations3MBlue  | Size - M, Color - Blue  |           | [Size:M,Color:Blue]  | 0               | 0        | false      |                       |
    When I update combination "productCombinations3SWhite" stock with following details:
      | delta quantity | 100 |
    Then combination "productCombinations3SWhite" should have following stock details:
      | combination stock detail   | value |
      | quantity                   | 100   |
      | minimal quantity           | 1     |
      | low stock threshold        | 0     |
      | low stock alert is enabled | false |
      | location                   |       |
      | available date             |       |
    And combination "productCombinations3SWhite" last stock movements should be:
      | employee   | delta_quantity |
      | Puffin Mummy | 100            |
    And combination "productCombinations3SWhite" last stock movement increased by 100
    When I update combination "productCombinations3SBlack" stock with following details:
      | delta quantity | 50 |
    Then combination "productCombinations3SBlack" should have following stock details:
      | combination stock detail   | value |
      | quantity                   | 50    |
      | minimal quantity           | 1     |
      | low stock threshold        | 0     |
      | low stock alert is enabled | false |
      | location                   |       |

That list is selected from the original Behat configuration, independently of the reference closure. The other suites' retained transforms and hooks are not globally registered. tests/UI (Playwright) and tests/Unit + tests/Integration PHPUnit are NOT part of behat.yml and are out of scope by construction.

Cross-scenario state inside a feature file — SharedStorage persists across scenarios, so customer_group_management.feature's 'Update the created customer group' presupposes the preceding 'Create' scenario ran. If a constructor argument cannot be autowired (Sylius wires many collaborators by service id, e.g. `@sylius.behat.api_platform_client.shop`, `@sylius.behat.api_platform_client.admin`, `@sylius.behat.shared_storage`), return an extra file named `behat_services.yml` containing a Symfony `services:` block with explicit `arguments:` for your classes.

facts: Step definitions are PHP 8 attributes on public context methods: `#[Given('/^regex$/')]`, `#[When(...)]`, `#[Then('plain text with :placeholder')]`. Both plain-text and `/^regex$/` patterns are used, and a single method may carry several attributes.
`#[Transform(...)]` methods on Transform contexts convert a captured string into an object, typically by repository lookup.
The scenario's `Background` steps run first; most are answered by the retained Setup contexts, but a few are answered only by the Api contexts you are writing.

Contexts are Symfony services. The harness registers every class you return as `public`, `autowired` and `autoconfigured`. If a constructor argument cannot be autowired (Sylius wires many collaborators by service id, e.g. `@sylius.behat.api_platform_client.shop`, `@sylius.behat.api_platform_client.admin`, `@sylius.behat.shared_storage`), return an extra file named `behat_services.yml` containing a Symfony `services:` block with explicit `arguments:` for your classes.

Requests are issued through the retained `Sylius\Behat\Client\ApiClientInterface` (`ApiPlatformClient`, wired over Symfony's `test.client`, in-process) together with `RequestFactoryInterface` and `ResponseCheckerInterface`. The shared clipboard between steps is `Sylius\Behat\Service\SharedStorageInterface` (`->set($key, $value)`, `->get($key)`).
Assertions are made with `Webmozart\Assert\Assert`.

Suites are tag-filtered and a scenario is reachable only through its suite: alongside the classes you return, the harness registers the retained Setup, Transform and Hook contexts of the API suite whose tag filter matches the scenario's feature tag plus `@api`.

Production namespaces are `Sylius\Component\*` and `Sylius\Bundle\*`. Put your classes under `src/Sylius/Behat/Context/Api/**`. Removal took that directory with the code, so it does NOT exist yet -- create the path you need.

feature.background:
Background:
        Given the store operates on a single channel in "United States"
        And that channel allows to shop using "English (United States)" and "Polish (Poland)" locales
        And the store has a product "Angel T-Shirt"
        And the store ships everywhere for Free
        And the store allows paying with "Cash on Delivery"
        And there is a customer "lucy@teamlucifer.com" that placed an order "#00000666"
        And the customer bought a single "Angel T-Shirt"
        And the customer "Lucifer Morningstar" addressed it to "Seaside Fwy", "90802" "Los Angeles" in the "United States" with identical billing address
        And the customer chose "Free" shipping method with "Cash on Delivery" payment
        And I am logged in as an administrator
feature.narrative:
In order to be able to send a lost email again
    As an Administrator
    I want to have the order confirmation email for a chosen order sent to the customer

        And the store has a text product attribute "Gun caliber"
        And the store has a text product attribute "Overall length"
        And the store has a non-translatable text product attribute "Author"
        And I am logged in as an administrator
feature.narrative:
In order to extend my merchandise with more complex products
    As an Administrator
    I want to add a new product with text attribute to the shop
feature.title: Adding a new product with text attribute

scenario.gherkin:
Scenario: Adding and removing text attributes on product create page
        When I want to create a new configurable product
        And I specify its code as "44_MAGNUM"
        And I name it "44 Magnum" in "English (United States)" locale
        And I set its slug to "44-magnum"
        And I add the "Gun caliber" attribute
        And I set the "Gun caliber" attribute value to "11 mm" in "English (United States)" locale
        And I add the "Overall length" attribute
        And I set the "Overall length" attribute value to "30.5 cm" in "English (United States)" locale
        And I remove its "Gun caliber" attribute
        And I add it
        Then I should be notified that it has been successfully created
        And the product "44 Magnum" should appear in the store
        And attribute "Overall length" of product "44 Magnum" should be "30.5 cm"
        And product "44 Magnum" should not have a "Gun caliber" attribute
scenario.title: Adding and removing text attributes on product create page

feature.background:
Background:
        Given the store operates on a single channel in "United States"
        And the store has a "Wyborowa Vodka" configurable product
        And there is a catalog promotion "Winter sale" with priority 1 that reduces price by "50%" and applies on "Wyborowa Vodka" product
        And there is a catalog promotion "Christmas sale" with priority 2 that reduces price by fixed "$5.00" in the "United States" channel and applies on "Wyborowa Vodka" product
        And the product "Wyborowa Vodka" has a "Wyborowa Vodka Exquisite" variant priced at "$40.00" and originally priced at "$15.00"
        And the product "Wyborowa Vodka" has a "Wyborowa Vodka Lemon" variant priced at "$10.00"
        And there is an exclusive catalog promotion "Extra sale" with priority 10 that reduces price by "10%" and applies on "Wyborowa Vodka Lemon" variant
        And I am logged in as an administrator
feature.narrative:
In order to be aware of historical variant prices
    As an Administrator
    I want to browse the catalog price history of a specific variant
feature.title: Seeing the price history of a product variant after changes to catalog promotions

scenario.gherkin:
Scenario: Seeing the catalog price history of a variant with many catalog promotions
        And I go to the price history of a variant with code "WYBOROWA_VODKA_EXQUISITE"
        Then I should see 2 log entries in the catalog price history
        And there should be a log entry on the 1st position with the "$5.00" selling price, "$15.00" original price and datetime of the price change
        And there should be a log entry on the 2nd position with the "$40.00" selling price, "$15.00" original price and datetime of the price change
scenario.title: Seeing the catalog price history of a variant with many catalog promotions

        Given the "Winter sale" catalog promotion is enabled

        And I go to the price history of a variant with code "WYBOROWA_VODKA"
